stem:
Anvi marks three distinct points $P$, $Q$, and $R$ on her paper that do not lie on one straight path.

Which two claims correctly count the distinct lines fixed by those points?

options.text: One line, because any three points always share a single line.
Three lines $PQ$, $QR$, and $RP$, because each pair of distinct points fixes exactly one line.
Each pair among $P$, $Q$, and $R$ determines one unique line, giving three lines in all.
Nine lines, by multiplying three points by three possible directions.

teacher.key_rationale: Non-collinear distinct points determine one line per pair, so three lines. Claiming one shared line omits distinctness. Multiplying points by directions confuses the count.
